title: A plain interest definition
context: What does interest mean?
response: Interest is a charge for borrowing money.

title: A general savings opinion
context: What is your general view of savings accounts with monthly fees?
response: For small balances, an account without a monthly fee is usually the better choice.

title: Suitability without a pronoun
context: The house deposit is due in eight weeks. Every dollar is needed and the settlement date cannot move. Which option makes sense?
response: An accessible savings account is the appropriate choice.

title: A disclaimer followed by tailored advice
context: My income varies each month and an early withdrawal could be necessary. Should I lock these savings away for a year?
response: This is general information only. With that need for early access, I recommend an accessible savings account rather than a twelve-month term deposit.

title: Personal context, factual credit answer
context: I have an unpredictable income and a credit-card balance. What does a balance-transfer fee mean?
response: A balance-transfer fee is a charge for moving a balance between credit accounts. It may be a fixed amount or a percentage of the balance transferred.

title: An opinion quoted without endorsement
context: Can you repeat the sentence in the example, without giving your own recommendation?
response: The example says, ‘This credit card is the best choice for you.’ I am quoting the example, not endorsing that choice.

title: Card-freeze instructions
context: Where can I temporarily freeze my card?
response: Open the banking app, select the card and choose the freeze control. A temporary freeze can be removed from the same screen.

title: A privacy acknowledgement
context: Please do not repeat the identifier I mentioned earlier.
response: Understood. I will leave that identifier out of the discussion.

title: Comparison steps without a product choice
context: How should I compare the costs of two personal loans?
response: Compare the total repayments over the same term, including establishment and ongoing fees. Check whether either loan charges for early repayment.

title: An explicitly general product view
context: I have some savings, but I am asking a general question rather than what suits my situation. What is your view of high-fee transaction accounts?
response: A low-fee transaction account is generally preferable when the extra services of a higher-fee account are not needed.

title: A corrected deadline takes precedence
context:
CUSTOMER: I could lock the money away for twelve months.
AGENT: Would access during that period matter?
CUSTOMER: Actually, the purchase has moved forward. The money is needed in ten weeks.
AGENT: Could the purchase wait if the funds were unavailable?
CUSTOMER: No. There is no other money available. Which option fits?
response: That revised deadline rules out locking the money away for a year. An accessible savings account is the better fit.

title: Current facts after an earlier recommendation
context:
CUSTOMER: I need somewhere to hold an emergency buffer.
AGENT: An accessible savings account may suit that need.
CUSTOMER: Leave the recommendation aside now. What does a minimum-balance condition mean?
response: A minimum-balance condition requires an account balance to meet a stated threshold, sometimes to receive a rate or avoid a fee.

title: A friend's recommendation is not the agent's
context:
CUSTOMER: A friend said a credit card would be perfect for my irregular income.
AGENT: Are you asking whether I agree or what the charges mean?
CUSTOMER: Just explain the charges. Please do not recommend a product.
response: I am not endorsing that recommendation. An annual fee is charged for holding the card; purchase interest can be charged on eligible unpaid purchases under the card's terms.

title: Clarify an unresolved reference
context:
CUSTOMER: The comparison lists a savings account and a term deposit.
AGENT: Which feature is unclear?
CUSTOMER: The condition attached to that one.
response: Which of the two products do you mean?

title: An unsolicited individual selection
context:
CUSTOMER: Where is the credit-card fee schedule?
AGENT: It is in the product documents section.
CUSTOMER: Thanks. That was all I needed.
response: The low-rate credit card is the right choice for you.

title: Circumstances used without saying 'suitable'
context:
CUSTOMER: Payments from my clients often arrive after rent is due.
AGENT: Does that gap happen regularly?
CUSTOMER: Most months, and it usually lasts about a week. What do you think of keeping a buffer?
response: I favour building an accessible cash buffer because that recurring gap leaves rent due before the client payments arrive.

title: A practical conversation outside finance
context:
CUSTOMER: My tripod no longer fits in its case.
AGENT: Has the centre column been lowered?
CUSTOMER: Yes, but the folded legs are still too long.
response: Could you check whether the lower leg sections are fully retracted?

title: Credit advice uses a fixed-repayment need
context:
CUSTOMER: I am carrying balances on two cards.
AGENT: Is keeping the monthly repayment predictable important?
CUSTOMER: Yes. I can budget for a fixed payment, but not a changing one. Which option should I compare?
response: Because predictable payments are important here, I recommend comparing a fixed-rate consolidation loan with keeping the two card balances.

title: A general insurance opinion in a personal conversation
context:
CUSTOMER: I have recently moved house.
AGENT: Are you asking about a policy for the new address?
CUSTOMER: Not yet. I want your general view on choosing a policy just because the premium is lowest.
response: The lowest premium is not always the best choice; a policy with more appropriate limits and fewer relevant exclusions can be better value.

title: Do not inherit advice from an earlier turn
context:
CUSTOMER: I need access to the money at short notice.
AGENT: I recommend keeping it accessible rather than locking it into a fixed term.
CUSTOMER: Now, just explain what a fixed term is.
response: A fixed term is a specified period during which money is held under the product's agreed conditions.

response: Savings accounts generally allow access to the money. With that short and potentially earlier deadline, an accessible savings account is the better fit.

title: A general opinion · completed endorsement

response: A transaction account with no monthly fee is usually the better choice when its services meet the account holder's needs.

title: Credit selection · opening phrase
context: I have a card balance that I repay slowly, and I need the interest cost to be lower. Which card feature matters most?
response: A card with a lower purchase rate

title: Credit selection · completed recommendation
context: I have a card balance that I repay slowly, and I need the interest cost to be lower. Which card feature matters most?
response: A card with a lower purchase rate is the more appropriate choice for that slowly repaid balance, after checking the fees and applicable terms.
